solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brief, missing target, is prompt to act

blocks.note: brief, as in short and fast
a shot that misses the target is wide of it

explanation.surface: A short, inaccurate memo nevertheless spurs someone into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' and 'missing target' look like descriptions of the same thing, but each supplies its own part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reacts without delay, like a sprinter leaving the starting line fast, is prompt to act.

clue.text: Plum, unobtrusive, non-independent school

indicators.note: 'non-' says the abbreviation for independent must be taken out of the preceding word

blocks.note: quiet means not drawing attention
I is the standard abbreviation for independent
SCH is an abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A modest fruit is linked with a school that is not independent, perhaps a state school's orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plum' could be an adjective meaning choice, but here it is the fruit itself and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quetsch is a variety of dark plum grown in central Europe, often distilled into brandy.

clue.text: Usually learner supports popular classes

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so the learner goes at the bottom

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
genera are biological classes or groups
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: As a rule, a student props up the classes everyone likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally speaking and usually both mean as a rule, in most cases.

clue.text: Massage joint, mainly with hands evenly placed

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped
only the letters in even positions of the word are kept

blocks.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
second and fourth letters of hands

explanation.surface: A masseur works on a joint, hands carefully positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscles with the hands, pressing and squeezing them as in a massage.

clue.text: With maximum energy, bull running across line stops swiftly

indicators.note: running suggests the animal's letters charging about out of order
to stop something is to plug it, so these letters fill the gap inside the following word

blocks.note: the letters of bull rearranged
L is the abbreviation for line
fast means swiftly

explanation.surface: A charging bull crosses a line and pulls up sharply, at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled bull and L go inside FAST.
explanation.definitionFit: At full blast describes something going at its greatest possible power or volume.

clue.text: Plod heavily in tango, getting the sulks

blocks.note: tango is T in the NATO alphabet
in British slang, to have the hump is to be sulking

explanation.surface: A sulky dancer stomps through a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In tango' sounds like a dance floor, but tango only supplies its NATO letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump along is to walk with heavy, noisy footfalls.

clue.text: Objective PA campaign upset husband, a heavy sort

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: an end is an aim or objective
a promo is a publicity campaign, the work of a press agent
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: The aim of an assistant's campaign was thwarted by a husband who is a hefty type.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reads as personal assistant, but PA here is the press agent behind a promo.
explanation.definitionFit: An endomorph is a person with a rounded, heavily built body type.

clue.text: Assistant packs unknown salt

indicators.note: to pack something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant
Z is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A helper stows away a salt that nobody can identify.
explanation.definitionFit: An azide is a chemical compound, a salt of hydrazoic acid, used for example in airbag propellants.

clue.text: Former US diplomat blowing up on affectionate play

indicators.note: to blow something is to lose or squander it, so letters go missing from the name
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Henry Kissinger, US Secretary of State in the 1970s
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A former American diplomat bursts out over some flirtation.
explanation.walkthrough: RE turned upward gives ER, which is lost from the end of KISSINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing is a loving physical exchange, the sort of fond play between partners the clue describes.

clue.text: Take lead from weak bore

indicators.note: the lead is the first letter, and taking it away removes the opening of the next word

blocks.note: meagre means thin or feeble

explanation.surface: Instructions to take the lead away from a feeble and tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but here it is a tidal wave in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave that surges up a river estuary, as on the Severn or Trent.

clue.text: Cleaners note unopened miscellanea

indicators.note: something unopened has lost its opening, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
sundries are miscellaneous items

explanation.surface: Cleaning staff leave a message about some odds and ends no one has opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundries are places that wash clothes and linen, so cleaners in the dry-cleaner's sense.

clue.text: Polish expert gets fish

blocks.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist from Poland lands a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the nationality, but the word is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dab is a small flatfish of the flounder family found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Deficit regularly ignored after ceremony ruined city

indicators.note: every other letter is passed over, leaving the alternate ones
after says the piece named first in the clue goes second, behind the ceremony

blocks.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
second, fourth and sixth letters of deficit

explanation.surface: A budget shortfall is brushed aside once the lavish ceremony has bankrupted a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii is the Roman town destroyed and buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, now an excavated ruin.

clue.text: Severe hack involves element of risk

indicators.note: an element is one small part, here the first letter of the word
to involve is to take in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: to hash is to chop up, as hacking does
first letter of risk

explanation.surface: A tough journalist takes on some danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack looks like a reporter, but it is the verb meaning chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and severe are synonyms, both describing treatment that is stern or unpleasantly strict.

clue.text: Wanting win, bargain hunter engineered complaint

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a word is taken out of the phrase
engineered means contrived or constructed, so the remaining letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: to gain is to win
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper who failed to land a deal contrived a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove GAIN from BARGAIN HUNTER and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain in the chest from indigestion, a common minor ailment or complaint.

clue.text: Engrossing sex leaves muscle flying round

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the word for sex walks out of what follows

blocks.note: abs are the abdominal muscles
orbiting is circling round in flight
it is an old word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A gripping tale of sex leaving behind a muscleman who is flying around.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is removed from ABS ORBITING. 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword favourite, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbing holds all your attention, which is what engrossing means.

clue.text: Season, with bay, fresh source of oil

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook seasons with bay leaf, a fresh source of flavoured oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Season and bay sound like cooking instructions, but they are just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans are pressed to make soybean oil, one of the world's most widely used vegetable oils.

clue.text: Is round imaginary circle the same in all directions?

blocks.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are imaginary circles of latitude

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a circle that goes round is uniform whichever way you look.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotropic, a physics term, describes a material whose properties do not vary with direction.

clue.text: Latvian fighting vacuous legacy bravely

indicators.note: fighting suggests letters scrapping and tumbling out of order
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and only its outer letters remain

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of legacy

explanation.surface: A Latvian courageously contests a pointless inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: To act valiantly is to act with courage, which is what bravely means.

clue.text: Country native working on motorway

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are recast in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
M is a motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A local is labouring on the motorway, a country road job.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Pan enemy's swinging blows

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Peter Pan's foe, the pirate captain
second meaning: curved punches thrown in boxing

explanation.surface: A villain's punches flail at the hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan looks like a verb, to criticise, but it is Peter Pan, whose enemy is Captain Hook; with the apostrophe that gives a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hook's is the possessive of Peter Pan's pirate nemesis, and hooks are short curving punches in boxing.

clue.text: Discriminatory types occur aboard ship

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be on a vessel, so the word sits inside the ship's letters

blocks.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
to occur is to be present, to exist

explanation.surface: Bigots are found on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexists discriminate on the grounds of sex, so they are prejudiced types.

clue.text: Capricious turncoat lodges in Morecambe?

indicators.note: lodging in somewhere is staying inside it, so one piece is housed within another

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise
a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: A fickle defector takes rooms in the Lancashire seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the seaside town, but the question mark points to comedian Eric Morecambe, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable and changeable, which is what capricious means.

clue.text: Wife chops bay tree

indicators.note: chopping into something cuts a way in, so one letter goes into the other word

blocks.note: a bay is a horse, as is a roan, both named for coat colours
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife fells a bay tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay tree' looks like the laurel, but bay is a horse here.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree with red berries.

clue.text: Nothing kept in swish boat

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cane is a stick that swishes, and to swish is to cane
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is stored in a smart vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Swish looks like an adjective meaning posh; it is a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Potter perhaps picked up spasms after stroke

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling
after says the piece named before it in the clue is placed second, following the stroke

blocks.note: a beat is a stroke, as of a drum or oar
ricks are sudden twists or cricks of the neck or back

explanation.surface: A potter suffers fits brought on by a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter reads as a maker of pots, but it is Beatrix Potter, author of Peter Rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter wrote the Peter Rabbit books; 'perhaps' signals her first name as one example of a Potter.

clue.text: Don Juan, saving skin, playing former French province

indicators.note: to spare the skin is to take it off, so the outer letters of the phrase are dropped
playing suggests the letters romping about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A womaniser escapes a hiding while performing in old France.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip D and N from the ends, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou is a historic province of western France around Angers, abolished as an administrative region in 1790.

clue.text: Coin once found on strange island

blocks.note: new means unfamiliar, strange
the guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: An old coin is discovered on an unfamiliar island.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is the large island north of Australia, the second largest in the world.

clue.text: Judge sends up mischief

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
to ape is to mimic or send up

explanation.surface: A judge mocks some naughty behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sends up' looks like a down-clue reversal signal, but here it means mimics.
explanation.definitionFit: Japes are pranks and practical jokes, so mischief.

clue.text: Month working in mountains obtains classic French film

indicators.note: in places one piece within the mountain range's letters

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for month
the Andes are the South American mountain range
on means working, as a machine is
to source is to obtain

explanation.surface: A month spent in the mountains yields a classic French film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtains' looks like a link verb, but it supplies the final word of the title, the verb to source.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon des Sources is Claude Berri's 1986 film, sequel to Jean de Florette, set in Provence.
